results.title: Late-season irrigation: Tips for yield protection and water stewardship
results.description:
Typically, corn at R2 (blister) uses approximately 6 to 7 inches of water to maturity; Soybeans at R4 (full pod) uses approximately 3 to 4 inches of water to maturity; and Potato at tuber bulking uses 4 to 5 inches of water to maturity. [...] As of early August, most irrigated corn in central and west-central Minnesota is close to the R2 growth stage. Soybeans are progressing through pod fill (R3–R5), with seed fill just beginning. These stages represent a critical period for grain yield determination. [...] Daily crop evapotranspiration (ETc) rates remain high at this time of the season, especially during hot and windy spells, but start declining after mid-August. Central Minnesota reference evapotranspiration (ETo) is averaging 0.20 inches/day, meaning soils can dry quickly if rainfall is limited.  
  
If soil moisture sensors or hand probes show dry conditions in the top 12–18 inches, strategic irrigation may still be warranted to protect kernel or seed fill.

requirements.missing: No document provides a specific decision rule or threshold for when to stop or reduce irrigation before chickpea harvest. Documents mention that irrigation can increase disease (Ascochyta blight) and that late irrigation may cause indeterminate flowering and poor quality, but no explicit cut-off timing, soil-moisture threshold, growth-stage trigger, or calendar rule is stated.

No quantitative preharvest irrigation cut-off values (e.g., kPa soil water potential, % volumetric water content, days after flowering, mm applied water) are provided for chickpea. Document s5 reports season-total ET and irrigation amounts (inches) for dryland vs deficit vs full irrigation treatments but does not give a preharvest stop criterion. Document s12 reports yield-per-mm water-use response slopes (kg ha⁻¹ mm⁻¹) but no harvest-time irrigation threshold. Geographic scope is limited to USA (Nebraska, Colorado, Montana).
